about: Chiara Condello grew up in Predappio, a hill village in the Apennine foothills southeast of Bologna, where her father Francesco founded the family estate, Condè, in 2001. After studying economics in Milan she came home and in 2015 started her own label, with her own vineyards and cellar. She farms about five hectares of Sangiovese, organic from the start, among woods and olive trees. Some scholars think Romagna may be where Sangiovese began, and she has become one of the leading young voices for it.

Le Lucciole (“the fireflies”) is her Riserva, from a single parcel of about 0.8 hectares of roughly 20-year-old, east-facing vines at about 250 metres. The soil is spungone, a Pliocene sandstone full of marine fossils. Her cellar work follows the late Giulio Gambelli. Grapes are partly destemmed and left as whole berries, then fermented with native yeasts in open-top wooden vats without temperature control, with macerations of about 45 days. The wine ages two years in old Slavonian oak casks and a year in bottle.

The result is pure Sangiovese with a light touch, savoury and fine-grained rather than heavy. Critics and her importers note red cherry, plum and wild strawberry, orange peel, violets and a hint of earth or leather, with firm but refined tannins and lively acidity. The long time in old casks and in bottle before release means it reaches the table already settled and open.
facts: About 0.8 ha single parcel, about 20-year-old vines, about 250 m
Native yeasts, open-top wooden vats, long maceration
24 months in old Slavonian oak casks, 12 months in bottle
